decisions.reason: The question covers real-world pedestrian–robot interactions but omits how the dataset could support pedestrian perception and motion prediction for social navigation.

Indoor and outdoor robot collection is stated. Manual operation, crowded locations in Seoul, the two 3D LiDARs and five cameras, pulse-per-second synchronization, and 360-degree camera coverage are missing.
The method gives 20-second sequences at 10 Hz. It omits the 60 scenes, 60K images, 12K point-cloud frames, 2D and 3D box annotations, object IDs, and multilayer semantic maps.
The poster omits robot ego-motion compensation and the use of different scenes across the training, validation, and test subsets.

The finding names all three comparison datasets and reports more SiT instances meeting both criteria. The finding and Figure 8 caption define the criteria as sharing semantic space and being within 2 meters of the robot or ego vehicle.
The detection and tracking baselines, the center-distance thresholds and averaging rule for detection mAP, and the tracking metrics are missing.

The poster gives 9 seconds of trajectory data per sample but omits the 2-second history and 7-second forecast split, minimum ADE and FDE over 5 and 20 candidates, the named baselines, and the semantic-map results for Y-Net and NSP-SFM.
The poster omits the end-to-end task of predicting future 3D boxes and trajectories from raw sensor data over 7 seconds, the baseline models and variants, and the four evaluation measures.
The poster omits the authors’ statement that time constraints prevented collection at the scale of hundreds of thousands of frames.
